title: Company Sues Over Trump's Taxes on Canadian Goods
summary:
On Tuesday, a lawsuit was filed in the U.S. Court of International Trade. It challenges President Donald Trump's tariffs on goods from Canada. A tariff is a tax on things brought in from another country.

The Liberty Justice Center, a nonprofit group, filed the case for Gellert Global Group, an American company that brings in food from other countries. The lawsuit says Trump went beyond his powers by using an old trade law from 1930, called Section 338.

Trump used that law to put a 50% tax on many Canadian goods after trade talks broke down in August. The White House says the law allows this. A Trump administration official said the government will defend the tariffs in court.

Gellert says the trade fight hurts it from both sides. It pays a 50% tariff on Canadian cheese, and Canada taxes the American cheese it sells there. Sara Albrecht of the Liberty Justice Center said shoppers in both countries are affected too.
why_it_matters: Tariffs can change the prices of foods and other things families buy.
